description: Diego's Cloud Store — the constellation app store as its own APK (#865). Hosts libs:appstore: the Cloud fleet list (install, update, download-all, auto-update on Wi-Fi), the phone's installed apps (stop, uninstall, sources) and the apps mesh. It also runs the background fleet pass that keeps every constellation app updated, Cloud SuperApp and itself included. Split out of cloud-superapp so the store ships and updates on its own.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

libs:perms.comment: #1274 the permission contract: the catalogue, PermsNeeds, PermsLink and PermsActivity, the Permissions page this app hosts for its libs (permissions are per package, so never another app's page).

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list. Every lib is shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs, the same directories cloud-superapp builds, so the store code exists once.

libs:sysdns._doc_dir: #874 FleetDnsBridge: app/build.gradle links this module as the one resolver of this process (1f36254d4), so settings.gradle must include it — this map is the gradle graph's single source of truth, and a dependency missing here is 'Project with path :libs:sysdns could not be found' at configuration time (the same gap SuperApp had, f3ca976c7).

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:shared-store._doc_dir: cloud-shared-store's store-access layer (contract). libs:appstore compiles it for the generated ICloudExec client: SharedUidMigration asks the OLD terminal build to back its home up over CLOUD_EXEC. Shared BY REFERENCE; reads ac_cloud-termux/build.json::shared_store.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ai._doc_dir: The top bar's AI panel: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) over the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only), the same chat Cloud Code's AI page has. Shared BY REFERENCE. This app holds no OpenRouter token and reads none (decisions-use guard D5): the gateway holds the fleet key. Its mesh address is baked as BuildConfig.AI_GATEWAY_URL by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle.

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency: the shared agent descriptor (assets/agents/agents.json) its Agent picker lists. Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

shizuku_client._doc: #894 Cloud Store's OWN privileged shell channel (owner decision 2026-10-07: the Store, not SuperApp, handles every fleet install and its own self-update). Read at build time by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle (BuildConfig.SHIZUKU_CLIENT_B64) exactly as cloud-termux's block is. The ladder ShellChannels walks is: the embedded wireless-adb client (paired once from Settings > Silent installs), our app_process server, then these providers in order. SuperApp's bridge is deliberately NOT listed: SuperApp stays out of the install pass, so this app must not depend on it for a channel.

privileged_channel._default_on_doc: Whether this app arms the privileged channel by itself (auto re-arm after reboot, when Wireless debugging is available, and before an install finds no channel). Cloud Store: ON so installs and updates work; the user turns it off on the ADB Shell page (Settings). Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools ChannelAutoArm.
privileged_channel._doc: What THIS app declares it needs the privileged shell channel for. Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle into BuildConfig.CHANNEL_NEEDS_B64 and listed, as written, in the Declared needs section of the ADB Shell page (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools AdbShellPage). Add a need here and it shows there; nothing about it is typed in Kotlin. Each need: id (unique), label, why (one sentence), commands (the shell verbs it runs).

needs.why: Access > Android Perms grants the fleet's missing runtime and signature permissions.

shizuku_diagnostics._doc: Only the per-app local server identity. The lib reads the CONSUMER's block first and falls back to SuperApp's whole block when absent, and SuperApp's app_process server binds 38099: two apps on one port means whichever starts second silently fails to bind. Cloud Store has no diagnostic bundles of its own.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

web._doc: #876 the store as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-store-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-store-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`, then diegonmarcos.github.io is told (repository_dispatch cloud-web-refresh). portal_slug is the tile's apps/<slug>/ folder on the cloud-web portal; entry is the page inside it. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds.

unit._doc: The shared top bar's Compose UI suite (libs:bottomnav AppTopBarTest, Robolectric, no emulator): the drawer a page supplies, the AI panel, the Settings dropdown, the Cloud Account launch intent and the Configs callback, run through THIS app because it is the first app to adopt AppTopBar. `storeUnitTests` (this app's root build.gradle) runs :libs:bottomnav (the top bar, the page strip, the Configs menu over the declared pages), :libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools (per-app ADB identity and state scope) and :libs:core (the notification matrix), and nothing else, so a sibling lib's suite cannot turn this release red. Run by the ship workflow's 'JVM unit tests' step, after the JDK/SDK and the vault key (this project cannot configure without the shared key), through build.sh test.

dns_handoff._doc: Cloud Store has no DNS page of its own: a failed Store row offers SuperApp's (page id dns, declared in aa_cloud-superapp/build.json). `package` is the app launched, `shortcut_action` the extra its launcher reads (ShellActivity.handleShortcutIntent). Baked into BuildConfig.DNS_HANDOFF_ACTION; kept here so the page id is not a literal this app's nav declaration would have to own.

ui._doc: #868 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island, ui.sections[] what each item opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. The island reads exactly Cloud, Phone, Search, Feed, Access and the app opens on Search (default_section). Settings is not an island item: it is the top bar's round Settings button (Account | Configs). #896/#896.3 child pages: Phone = Installed | Declared (Search is its own island item, hosted by the same libs:appstore StorePhoneFragment on its search page), Feed = Commits | CI-CD (ids = appstore-feeds.json feed ids), Access = Apps Mesh | IPC | Identity | Android Perms | Cloud Perms (#ipc: IPC is the fleet's IPC Mesh, libs:appstore IpcMeshPage, the same page SuperApp > Configs > Network > IPC draws; Identity is libs:appstore FleetIdentityPage, the same page SuperApp > Configs > Apps Mesh > Identity draws: each fleet app's Linux uid, its sharedUserId group from data/fleet-identity.json, the live uid and signer, and any mismatch). MainActivity draws them with PageTabs and StorePages tells the pages below which is open; a host with no strip (SuperApp's embedded Store) gets Phone's drawn by the fragment. Cloud keeps its data-driven group tabs (one per constellation group, so not declared here) and nothing else: Apps Mesh and Perms moved to Access, Commits and CI-CD to Feed.

top_bar._doc: THE first row of the app (libs:bottomnav AppTopBar, declared once for the fleet): a hamburger that opens a side drawer the CURRENT page fills (MainActivity's StoreDrawer: the Store's sections and the open section's pages), the title, and two circular buttons: AI (libs:ai's chat in an anchored panel) and Settings (Account launches Cloud Account, Configs opens the Settings section below). Settings left the island for the top bar's Settings > Configs, which is a PAGE with its own top tabs (Sources | ADB Shell | AI | Notifications | About, the `settings` section's pages below, drawn by PageTabs and filled by ConfigsPage; test-store-configs-pages.sh holds the set): the section stays declared (it is the page Configs opens, and `tab=settings` still lands on it) but is no longer a bottom_nav id. No app draws its own copy of this row (cloud-android-top-bar-guard).

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Install and update every Cloud app
about.description: Cloud Store is the fleet's app store. It lists every Cloud app, installs one from the signed release CI builds for each commit, updates installed apps (automatically on Wi-Fi when enabled), shows what this phone runs, the feed of commits and CI runs, and the access page (mesh, MCP, IPC, identity and permissions). It exists so no app comes from a third-party store and the phone always runs what the repository says.

about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

Receives this app's crash reports on the phone.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
